overview: Aqua 13's Scaffold is a full block-placing module built around a single onEvent dispatcher. Every tick it runs a block search (find) that picks the best support block around the player, synchronizes the hotbar slot through the EventSycItem event so the client sends the C09 held-item change, forces the rotation through EventPreMotion (either a static 180/82 look or a calculated aim from rotationrecode2), and places through the vanilla player controller, which emits C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement. Swings are either local (swingItem) or sent as C0APacketAnimation. Six tower modes (Cubecraft, Watchdog, UpdatedNCP, WatchdogNew, IntaveFast, VerusFast) each implement a different jump profile, and VerusFast also spams fake C08 packets. The module carries its own HUD (block count with three shader styles), a block ESP, a blacklist of non-placeable block ids, timer abuse (BMCBoost at 1.105x), Down and SameY bridging, and a LegitPlace mode that reimplements the vanilla right-click pipeline.

sections.p: Scaffold extends Module and subscribes to seven events through one onEvent(Event) method: RenderNameTags (block ESP), Tick (off-ground counter), Render2D and PostRender2D (block count HUD), SycItem (hotbar slot sync), Update (search, tower, sprint and placement), and PreMotion (rotation override). All settings are registered through Aqua.setmgr with the Hero Setting framework, and the placement result is stored in the static BlockData inner class so every method can read it without passing arguments. The BlackList inner class filters block ids so non-full blocks never get placed.

Six tower modes are dispatched from the update pass when the jump key is held: Cubecraft (0.42 hop every 50ms), Watchdog (0.409 jump with a damped impulse on the third air tick), UpdatedNCP (0.4196 impulse on %3==1 air ticks, with a separate moving profile), WatchdogNew (the same impulse while moving only), IntaveFast (0.405 jump damped on the fifth air tick), and VerusFast, which sends fake C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement packets (an invalid -1,-1,-1 position and a position 1.5 blocks below the player) and rides a 0.70096 vertical boost. BMCBoost runs the client timer at 1.105x while a speed potion is active. Down mode lowers the placement level to posY - 1 while sneaking, SameY keeps the level from enable time, and sprint handling has a dedicated Intave branch.

find() searches the six neighbors of the block below the player, then an 8-cell ring one and two blocks out, accepting only solid blocks whose attach point is not occluded by a 10-step ray trace. getBlockSlot() picks the first hotbar slot holding a non-blacklisted ItemBlock, and EventSycItem forces that slot into the client so the held-item change (C09PacketHeldItemChange) precedes each placement. EventPreMotion overrides the outgoing rotation: Static mode sets yaw + 180 and pitch 82, Calculated mode uses rotationrecode2 (atan2 aim, sensitivity snapping, pitch clamped to 78-80, optional ReverseYaw and YawPosition tuning). Placement runs through the vanilla player controller, and the swing is either swingItem or a direct C0APacketAnimation. LegitPlace reimplements the vanilla right-click mouse pipeline with the 4-tick delay.

annotations.text: Package declaration: the Scaffold module lives in Aqua's world module package next to Eagle and BedFucker.
Settings framework import: Aqua uses the Hero settings system (de.Hero.settings.Setting), the same framework every module registers its toggles through.
Event system core: the Event base class and the EventType enum (PRE/POST) that splits the update pass into phases.

Event listener imports: the seven event classes Scaffold subscribes to. EventSycItem is Aqua's held-slot sync event, and EventPreMotion carries the rotation override into the outgoing movement packet.

Client internals: the Aqua singleton for settings access, ThemeScreen state, the Category and Module bases, the Killaura and Fly modules (target state and teleport helpers), the visual modules used by the HUD, and the RandomUtil, RenderUtil, RotationUtil and TimeUtil helpers.
Java standard imports: AWT Color for the HUD tints, ArrayList and List for the position history and blacklist.

Minecraft imports: block classes and states, the client, chat and resolution classes, GL state management, the Items and Blocks used by the VerusFast tower, ItemBlock for slot detection, the C08 placement and C0A animation packets, Potion for the speed boost, and the Vec3, BlockPos, EnumFacing, MathHelper and MovingObjectPosition geometry types.
LWJGL import: GL11 constants used directly in the BlockESP render path (blend, line smooth, depth and texture toggles).
Class declaration: Scaffold extends Module, Aqua's module base, and is registered under Module.Type.World.
espPos: the block position highlighted by the BlockESP overlay, cached from the last full block below the player.
blackList: an inner-class instance holding the block ids that must never be used as scaffold material.
rots: the calculated rotation pair, exposed publicly so other modules can read the current aim.
lastRots: the previous rotation pair, kept for modules that need the delta between ticks.
slot: the hotbar slot currently holding a usable block, synchronized with the client through EventSycItem.
objectPosition: the raycast result cache, reset every PRE update and read by the render pass.
lastPositions: an ArrayList of Vec3 that is declared but never written to anywhere in the file; leftover state from an earlier revision.
xyz: a double[3] field that is likewise never used; dead code.
data: the static BlockData holder (facing plus position) shared across the module. Static because the inner BlockData class stores its values in static fields.
timeUtil: the cooldown clock reused by every tower mode and the Cubecraft jump gate.
posY: the y level used for Down-mode placement, snapped to posY - 1 while sneaking.
down: the Down-mode state flag that remembers whether the player is currently bridging downward.
offGround: a tick counter of air ticks since the last grounded tick, the core signal for the NCP-family tower modes.
Constructor: calls the Module base with the name, type, description, keybind 0 and the World category, then registers every setting through Aqua.setmgr.
Sprint toggle: keeps the sprint key held while scaffolding. EnableCalculate toggle: on enable, snaps the head rotations to pitch 82 and yaw 180 to seed the Calculated rotation mode.
EnableSneak (forces the sneak key while the module is on), BlockCount (the blocks-in-hotbar HUD), BlockESP (the highlighted block under the player).
Intave toggle, read by the sprint and placement branches to switch behavior on Intave anticheat servers. Swing toggle: plays swingItem locally instead of sending the C0A packet.
Down: bridge downward while sneaking. SameY: bridge straight ahead at the recorded y instead of at the player's feet.
Expand: push the search position ahead by the Expandlength value. AutoDisable: turn the module off the moment Killaura acquires a target.
BMCBoost: the timer abuse that speeds the client tick up to 1.105 while a speed potion is active. LegitPlace: the alternate placement path that mimics vanilla right-click behavior.
ReverseYaw: invert the Calculated yaw so the player faces away from the block instead of toward it.
SneakModify number setting: declared but never read anywhere in the module; a leftover from a planned sneak-speed adjustment.
Expandlength: how many blocks ahead of the player the Expand search position is pushed (0-25, default 8).
YawPosition: the angle subtracted from the atan2 yaw in Calculated mode (default 90), tuning where the player looks relative to the block.
RotationMode: Static uses a fixed 180 yaw and 82 pitch; Calculated uses the block-derived aim from rotationrecode2.
Shader: picks the HUD backdrop renderer (Glow, Shadow or Jello) for the block count display.
Tower: the six tower mode strings, each an anticheat-specific jump profile implemented later in onEvent.
onEnable override: the enable hook for the module.
EnableCalculate seed: when the setting is on, the head yaw and pitch fields are forced to 180 and 82 so the first Calculated rotation starts from a known pose instead of the player's current look.
Resets the off-ground tick counter; a fresh session must not inherit air time from the previous one.
EnableSneak: holds the vanilla sneak key down for the whole session, the cheap way to keep the player's hitbox small while bridging.
Snapshots posY at enable time; SameY and Down placement reference this stored level instead of the live position.
super.onEnable(): lets the module base run its own enable bookkeeping (event subscription and so on).
onDisable override: the disable hook for the module.
Restores timerSpeed to 1.0, undoing any BMCBoost or VerusFast timer manipulation.
Releases the sneak key so it does not stay stuck after disable.
super.onDisable(): base-class cleanup.
onEvent(Event): the single dispatch point for every subscribed event, one big if-chain over the event types.
RenderNameTags guard: the ESP path only runs on the name-tag render event while BlockESP is enabled.
Tracks the block directly below the player; espPos only updates when that block is a full block, otherwise the previous highlight is kept.
Null check: nothing is drawn until a valid espPos exists.

GL state setup for the ESP box: enable blending with standard alpha factors and line smoothing, disable the depth test and texturing, disable face culling and clear the depth mask so the box renders as an overlay.
Reads the client HUD color from the settings manager to tint the box.
Draws the ESP box inside a Blur.drawBlurred lambda so the outline is rendered against a blurred backdrop.
Second direct pass of the box with a fixed 0.392 alpha, giving the highlight a filled face on top of the blurred outline.
GL state teardown: restores color, depth mask, culling, texturing, depth test and blend state in reverse order so the rest of the frame renders cleanly.
EventTick guard: the off-ground counter runs on the client tick event.
Increments offGround while airborne and resets it to 0 on the first grounded tick. The tower modes read this counter to time their mid-air impulses.
Render2D guard: the block count HUD draws on the 2D render event while BlockCount is enabled.
Builds the scaled resolution and skips drawing while the animated chat is open so the counter does not overlap chat.

Jello HUD branch: when the Shader mode is Jello and the theme hero screen is not active, the counter and a small triangle are drawn twice, first through ShaderMultiplier.drawGlowESP for the glow pass and then as solid rounded rects and text using the novolineSmall font.
Shadow fallback: the same counter layout drawn with Shadow.drawGlow around the rounded rect and triangle, then the plain rects and text on top.
Second Render2D block: a separate HUD branch for the theme-hero and non-Jello shader layouts.
Theme hero branch: draws a compact counter box next to the crosshair (offset from screen center) with the roboto2 font, a black backing rect and a thin green underline rect.

Shadow and Glow branch: for non-Jello shaders the 'Blocks:' text box is drawn under the crosshair, either through Shadow.drawGlow or ShaderMultiplier.drawGlowESP depending on which shader is selected.
Blur pass: the backing rounded rect is rendered again inside Blur.drawBlurred with a translucent black fill so the text stays readable over the world.
PostRender2D guard: the final HUD pass draws after the main 2D render.
Condition chain: the box only renders when BlockCount is on, the shader is not Jello, the theme hero screen is not active, and the shader is Shadow or Glow.
Draws the translucent black backing rect centered below the crosshair.
Draws the 'Blocks : N' text with the comfortaa4 font at the same position.
EventSycItem guard: runs when the client syncs the held slot, but only when a valid block slot exists.
Forces both the event and the module slot to getBlockSlot(), so the client's slot-change machinery sends the C09PacketHeldItemChange with the scaffold slot before each placement.
EventUpdate PRE guard: the first update pass of the tick.
Clears the cached raycast result; it is recomputed fresh every tick.
Runs the initial block search with a zero offset and stores the result in the static data holder.

Second EventUpdate pass: recomputes the block data so the value is fresh by placement time. BMCBoost: while a speed potion is active and the setting is on, the client timer runs at 1.105x, moving the player faster than the server expects between placements; without the potion the timer is forced back to 1.0.
AutoDisable: if Killaura currently has a target, the module switches itself off so scaffold rotations never fight the aimbot's.
Tower dispatch: the Cubecraft mode only acts while the jump key is held. Every 50ms the vertical motion is set to 0.42, a repeatable low hop that stays under the anticheat's jump cap.
Cubecraft ground assist: while standing on the freshly placed block (checked 0.1 blocks below), the same 0.42 impulse is reapplied to keep the hop chain alive.
Watchdog tower guard: active while the jump key is held, a grounded jump at 0.409 vertical motion.
Watchdog air control: on the third airborne tick the motion is damped by a small random factor (around 0.9909), breaking the exact-repetition pattern NCP-style checks look for.

UpdatedNCP tower guard: jump-key only. While not moving, the tower only jumps on ticks where ticksExisted % 3 == 1 after at least one air tick, using a 0.4196 impulse; the timeUtil gate (2000ms) throttles how often the pattern restarts.
UpdatedNCP moving branch: mirrors the Watchdog profile (0.409 grounded jump, damped impulse on the third air tick) so the player can tower while walking.

WatchdogNew guard: the newest Watchdog profile, jump key plus forward movement required. It fires the same 0.4196 impulse on the %3==1 air tick with the 2000ms time gate and no standstill branch; it only acts while moving.

IntaveFast guard: jump held and forward key released, the anti-strafe condition Intave expects. Grounded jump at 0.405 vertical motion, tuned lower than the NCP profiles, and on the fifth air tick the motion is damped by a 0.9909 random factor with a smaller 0.08 subtraction, keeping vertical speed inside Intave's accepted window.
VerusFast guard: no jump-key requirement; the mode activates purely by being selected.

VerusFast: while the jump key is held, a fake C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement is sent for the invalid block position (-1,-1,-1) with facing 255, the bucket-click trick Verus's placement check fails to validate. A second C08 aimed at a position 1.5 blocks below the player carries a stone itemstack, forcing the server to accept the vertical placement.

VerusFast boost: while the 5000ms time gate has not elapsed, vertical motion is set to 0.70096, a much higher jump than any legit profile, since the fake placements keep the anticheat from flagging the ascent. When the jump key is released the timer is restored to 1.0 so timer abuse is not left active.
Resets the time gate on every tick, so while the jump key is held the 5000ms branch never fires and the 0.70096 boost applies every tick.
Sprint guard: the DisablerModes setting switches between the normal and Intave sprint paths.
Normal sprint: while the Sprint setting is on the sprint key is held; otherwise sprinting is explicitly cleared.
Intave sprint: sprinting is only forced while the Sprint setting is on and the jump key is released; while jumping or with the setting off, sprint is cleared.
Placement guard: the non-legit path runs unless LegitPlace is on.
SameY branch: an empty block body; the SameY position logic already ran inside find(). Dead code that only shows where the mode hooks in.
Down mode: while sneaking, the target y is set to posY - 1 and the down flag is raised; releasing sneak restores the normal level. find() reads this stored y during the search.
Recomputes block data a third time right before placement so the latest position and facing are used.
Placement guard: only proceeds when a block target exists and a usable block is in the hotbar.
Reads the current mouse-over block and ticks the player controller, keeping the client-side interaction state in sync.
Computes the hit vector: the block center plus half a block along the facing direction, the point the server expects in the placement packet.

Right-click dispatch: calls onPlayerRightClick with the current slot's stack, the target position, facing and hit vector, which sends the actual C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement through the vanilla pipeline. The slot != -1 guard prevents a null-stack crash.

Swing handling: with the Swing setting on the client plays the arm animation locally (swingItem); otherwise the raw C0APacketAnimation is queued so the server sees the swing without the client re-rendering it.
Dead code: a fresh BlockPos from the mouse-over is assigned to a local variable and never used.
LegitPlace branch: the vanilla-mimicking path starts here.
Recomputes block data and takes the block directly below the player as the placement anchor.

Sneak emulation: when the block below is air the sneak key is forced on (the player shifts over the edge, vanilla-style), and off otherwise, except on Intave servers where the forced sneak is skipped.
Jump handling: while the jump key is held, sprinting is cleared so the jump does not turn into a sprint-jump.
Sprint suppression: with a speed potion active or the Sprint setting off, both the sprint state and the sprint key are cleared.
Placement: when the block below is air, rightClickMouse places the block from the current slot, exactly like a vanilla right-click.
Sneak key sync: while jumping the sneak key is held; otherwise it mirrors whether the block below is air.
PreMotion guard: rotation overrides only run when a block target exists.
Null guard: without block data the module returns early and leaves rotations untouched. Otherwise the aim is computed from the current block data through rotationrecode2.
Static mode guard: the fixed-rotation profile.
Static mode: the client rotation helpers are seeded from the head angles, then the outgoing EventPreMotion yaw is forced to rotationYaw + 180 and pitch to 82, the classic straight-down scaffold look.
Calculated mode guard: the block-derived profile.

Calculated mode: seeds the rotation helpers from the head angles and overrides the event's yaw and pitch with the values from rotationrecode2, which are then baked into the next C03PacketPlayer movement packet.
getPositionByFace: helper that returns the attach point on a block face, used by the raycast visibility check.

Builds the half-block offset along the face direction so the attach point sits half a block outside the block center on that face, adds the target block's center, and returns the center plus the face offset, the point a placement ray would hit.
rayTrace: tests whether the segment from the eye position to the attach point is blocked by a solid block, so the module only picks placements it can actually see.
Fixed step count: 10 subdivisions for the segment. The per-step delta along each axis is computed and the walk starts at the origin.
Samples a block position at each step and reads its block state.
Skips liquids and air; only solid blocks can occlude the placement ray.
Gets the collision bounding box for the sampled block.
Null boxes (non-colliding blocks) are replaced with an empty box so the containment test below cannot throw.
If the step point falls inside the block's world-space collision box, the ray is blocked and the placement is rejected.
Ray finished without hitting anything solid: the placement is visible.
find: the block search, called three times per tick with an offset vector.
Horizontal velocity from the position delta since the last tick, and the Expandlength read. Expand: the search x is pushed ahead by velocity times the expand length; otherwise the player's x is used.

Y selection: unless SameY or Down is active the search uses the live y; otherwise it uses the stored posY while the forward key is held, letting those modes bridge at a fixed level. The same projection applies to z.

The inverted facing table: for a block at a given direction, the face the placement must click is the opposite face. The base search position is the player's position (plus offset) shifted one block down, the spot the scaffold fills.
First pass: checks all six neighbors of the base position, starting with the candidate neighbor position.
Accepts a neighbor only if it is not air and the attach point is not occluded by the ray trace.
Returns the BlockData: the inverted facing and the neighbor position, meaning place against that neighbor to fill the base spot.
Second pass offsets: an 8-entry ring around the base position (one and two blocks out on each axis) for placements when no direct neighbor works.
Second pass: iterates the ring offsets, building each ring candidate position at the same y.
Only considers ring cells that are currently air, i.e. spots that still need filling.
For each air cell, checks all six of its neighbors in turn.
Accepts the neighbor if it is solid and visible, exactly like the first pass.
Returns the BlockData for the ring placement.
No placement found anywhere: returns null and the placement path skips this tick.
getBlockSlot: scans the nine hotbar slots for the first usable block.
Reads the stack in the current hotbar slot and requires a non-null stack whose item is an ItemBlock, i.e. a placeable block item.
Blacklist check: resolves the item registry id (for example minecraft:stone) and rejects it if the BlackList contains it, so slabs and chests are never chosen as scaffold material.
Returns the winning slot index.
No usable block in the hotbar: returns -1, which the callers treat as do-not-place.

mouseSens: snaps a yaw/pitch pair to the mouse sensitivity grid, mirroring the vanilla smoothing formula. The sensitivity cube is the base of Minecraft's mouse delta math: yaw snaps to the coarser step and pitch to the finer step (sensitivity squared).
Returns the snapped pair.
updateRotation: vanilla-style gradual rotation, moving current toward needed by at most speed degrees.
Wraps the angular difference into [-180, 180] and clamps positive overshoot to the speed limit.
Clamps negative overshoot to the speed limit.
Returns the incremented rotation.
rotationrecode2: the Calculated-mode aim. x is the target block center plus half the facing offset, relative to the player.

Same computation for z, the aim height 0.6 above the target block (roughly head height of a standing player), the vertical delta from the player's eye level, and the horizontal distance that forms the base of the pitch triangle.
Yaw: with ReverseYaw the atan2 angle is flipped 270 degrees (facing away); otherwise the YawPosition setting is subtracted, letting the user rotate the look around the block.
Pitch from the eye-to-target triangle, looking down at the block.
Normalizes negative yaw into [0, 360).
Snaps yaw and pitch to the mouse sensitivity grid (same formula as mouseSens).
Returns the pair with pitch clamped into 78-80 degrees, the tight window that keeps the placement ray on the block face without looking straight down.

rightClickMouse: the vanilla right-click pipeline reimplemented for LegitPlace mode. It skips entirely if the controller is mid-swing and sets the vanilla right-click delay timer to 4 ticks so the client does not spam clicks faster than legit input.
Try block: the whole interaction runs under a null guard (the mouse-over can briefly hold nulls during world swaps) and switches on the mouse-over hit type.
ENTITY case: delegates to the controller's entity interaction; the empty body means a successful interact is intentionally ignored here.
BLOCK case: reads the mouse-over block position and only interacts with non-air materials; clicking through air is skipped.
Null-stack guard: with an empty hand the item is simply not used (the boolean assignment is dead code).
Sends the placement through onPlayerRightClick, which emits the C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement.
Swing handling: with the Swing setting off the C0APacketAnimation is queued directly; otherwise swingItem plays the local animation.
Second null-stack guard: exits early when the hand is empty.
Slot cleanup: when the stack is fully consumed the hotbar slot is emptied.
NullPointerException sink: mouse-over races are swallowed silently, matching vanilla's own crash protection.

getBlockCount: totals every block item in the hotbar for the HUD counter by scanning the nine hotbar slots, reading each stack and adding the stack size only for non-null stacks carrying an ItemBlock.
Returns the running total.
isOnGround: box-cast check; true when a collision box exists within height blocks below the player.
BlackList inner class: holds the registry ids of blocks the scaffold must never place.
The id list, created empty and filled in the constructor, which registers every banned id.

The ban list: slabs (which would not make a solid floor), banners, beacons, chests, trapped chests, anvils, enchanting and crafting tables, furnaces, the three banner variants, cobwebs and saplings. These blocks break the bridge, are non-full, or are decorative, so the module skips them even when they are in the hotbar.
Getter for the id list, kept for completeness (never called in this file).
Blacklist check: a block id is usable when it is not in the list.
Registers a new banned id.
BlockData static class: the module-wide placement record (facing plus position).
Static fields for facing and pos: static because the module reads them through Scaffold.BlockData.getFacing() and getPos() from several methods without an instance. The constructor stores the pair.
Assigns the static facing and position. Because the fields are static, every find() call overwrites the previous result for the whole module.
Static facing getter.
Static position getter.
